pos.personaBrief: Madrid won knockout ties with less possession than opponents (Flashscore) and Ancelotti says there is no single Madrid identity, so ball control is not a goal in itself; freedom applies once players have the ball.

pro.personaBrief: Ancelotti builds with a 3-3 shape and Modric/Kroos dropping, but happily goes direct to Benzema and tells players to decide with the ball; he does not demand forward-only or fixed patterns.

est.personaBrief: Freedom is the core: Vinicius and Rodrygo roam as they feel, players self-organise to cover zones (Sky, Flashscore), Ancelotti does not know if it was 4-3-3 or 4-4-2, and Benzema drops deep.

lar.personaBrief: Ancelotti lets wide players drift inside or stay wide by their own reading and lets both full-backs push, using a mix of routes rather than a doctrine; he has used extra central midfielders with Camavinga, Modric and Kroos.

blo.personaBrief: Madrid pressed little, used a mid-block and sometimes a low block against strong teams (Coaches' Voice, Flashscore, Ancelotti 2022), so compactness is non-negotiable but high pressing is not the identity.

mar.personaBrief: Compact principles and players covering zones (Flashscore) point to zonal defending, with no evidence of dedicated man-markers; Vinicius cheats in transition instead of being tied to a marking task.

pla.personaBrief: Ancelotti said Madrid would have no singular identity, with low blocks in some matches, and shaped the team around the players he had; Scaloni also changes system at any moment. Adaptation to opponent and squad beats imposing a model.

res.personaBrief: A pragmatic winner: Madrid won Champions Leagues with less possession and a mid or low block, fresh subs around the 70th minute; freedom serves winning, not spectacle for its own sake.

sis.personaBrief: Freedom is the tactic: stars like Vinicius and Bellingham are trusted to make the difference and are not tied to a role or tracking duties, while systems are kept light and too much information is said to kill creativity.

jog.personaBrief: Trusted technical veterans such as Modric, Kroos and Benzema carried the teams, with Madrid not pressing or leaning on physical intensity; quality on the ball was the key asset.

bas.personaBrief: Zidane kept 10 of 11 finalists and stayed loyal to big names, and Ancelotti blended world-class experience with young talent; titles rely on seasoned stars, with youngsters rotated in.

lid.personaBrief: Authority is built through relationships: Zidane says 70 per cent is social competence and players must like you, Ancelotti gives freedom and short video sessions, though lateness is dealt with by talking first and acting only if the reason is unacceptable.
